sealed.statement: A verifier rejection must stay recordable after the repair it demands, and a doneWhen bar that only grows must not need a rejection finding at all: bind rejection findings to the sealed review manifest rather than to current worktree bytes, add a monotone receipt-bar-strengthen amendment, and validate scope before bytes so the refusal message names the actionable flag.

constraints.statement: This is a process Quest: it changes scripts/solve*, its tests and docs only. No src/ file changes, and no runtime behaviour of the database itself is touched.

A verifier-rejection finding validates its fingerprint against the sealed review manifest (solve/state/reviews/<id>.json manifest.candidate/aggregate fingerprint), which is immutable once minted, rather than against current worktree bytes. This makes a rejection recordable after the repair it demanded, because the referent is what WAS verified, not what is present now.

receipt-bar-strengthen accepts only a strict superset of the sealed requiredReceipts on the same probe and the same receipt file. It can never remove, rename or rewrite a receipt, never change doneWhen.probe, and therefore needs no verifier-rejection finding: it can only make the bar harder.

A strengthened bar updates the frontier metric args as well as doneWhen args wherever they share the probe and receipt file, because the test-receipt probe measures only requiredReceipts; strengthening doneWhen alone would raise a bar that nothing measures.

Scope validity is checked before any current-bytes comparison, so the refusal a caller sees names the actionable flag and does not depend on whether the quest happens to have candidate-contract attempts.

Existing recorded amendments and rejection findings keep their meaning; the existing amendment kinds, the amendment limit, and the evidence-linkage rule for verifier-driven kinds are unchanged, proven by controls that must stay green.
Proof is a deterministic node:test witness on temp roots, red on HEAD and green after, with existing-amendment-kinds-unchanged and existing-rejection-flow-unchanged as controls that must stay green.

hypothesis: Bind verifier-rejection findings to the sealed review manifest instead of current worktree bytes (--review), add the monotone receipt-bar-strengthen amendment kind that needs no rejection finding, raise the sealed frontierMetrics alongside doneWhen so the bar actually binds, and validate rejection scope before any bytes comparison so the refusal names the actionable flag.

evidence: verifier review-859df3428d6d67059b0f2f37 F-1/F-2: two receipts could not fail; these two bind the scope reorder and the foreign-quest guard

problems: system theory required after repeated same-frontier stalls

problem: This frontier stalled three times for one recurring reason: receipts whose durable claim exceeded what they asserted. Round 1 shipped two receipts that could not fail (scope-validated-before-bytes was satisfied by the pre-change code because the fixture had no candidate-contract attempt, so the bytes branch never ran; the foreign-quest guard had no scenario at all). Round 2 shipped a receipt whose detail text claimed duplicate and non-string ids were refused when no assertion covered either, and left the only intrinsics defense in the change (ownValue) with no fixture.
successCondition: Every guard the change adds reds at least one receipt when removed, and every receipt detail names only what its assertions prove. Confirmed for all three previously-green mutations: uniqueStrings type/empty guard, uniqueStrings duplicate guard, and ownValue weakened to a plain inherited read each now red exactly one scenario (13 pass / 1 fail), with the baseline at 14/0.
mechanism: Two compounding causes. (1) Authoring: I wrote the receipt detail from the INTENT of the code change rather than from the assertions actually present, so the durable claim and the proof drifted apart at write time. (2) Editing: I patched the witness with plain string replacement that silently no-ops on a miss, and eslint --fix had already rewritten the object keys to quoted form, so my unquoted pattern matched nothing. I then verified only the aggregate scenario count (14/14 green), which cannot distinguish an applied edit from a skipped one. Both causes are invisible to a green run and only a mutation matrix exposes them.
decidingOwner: The quest author. The Solver already provides the discriminating tool: doneWhen requiredReceipts plus a per-guard mutation. Nothing in the tooling failed here.
missingTransitionOrObservation: Nothing enforces that a receipt's detail text is backed by its assertions, and nothing runs a per-guard mutation matrix. Both are currently supplied only by an independent verifier, which is why all three rounds were caught downstream of authoring rather than at it.
discriminator: Run the mutation, not the suite. A guard whose removal leaves the bar fully green is not covered, regardless of how many receipts pass. Aggregate count is not evidence that an edit applied; assert that each replacement matched before writing the file.
